messages.author: 5ccb721d28384a05
messages.subject: MSstatsPTM removing unmodified peptides
parts:
Hello,

I was wondering if you could offer any advice on what to do with unmodified peptides in a PTM-enriched dataset when performing MSstatsPTM.

Briefly, I have a diGly enriched proteome and a whole peptide proteome which were run separately. The whole peptide proteome datasets was analysed using MSstatsTMT, and both datasets were analysed using MSstatsPTM. For MSstatsPTM, the whole peptide proteome was utilised as the 'unmodified dataset' which is being used to adjust against the diGly enriched dataset during the groupComparisonPTM stage (as recommended in the paper). 

This is working well for MSstatsPTM, however it does mean I end up with both diGly modified and unmodified peptides that were present in the diGly enriched proteome. As I am only interested in the diGly modified peptides when performing MSstatsPTM, these peptides are of no value.

I was wondering what the best course of action is for removing these unmodified peptides.

1. Should they be removed at all?
2. If they can be removed, when is it best to remove them i.e. should they be removed before protein summarisation, or before groupComparisonPTM or should they be left until after MSstatsPTM analysis is performed and then removed after. 

At the moment I have removed the unmodified peptides after protein summarisation by using this code:

MSstats.SF.diGly.Protein <- quant.msstats.SF$PTM[["ProteinLevelData"]]
MSstats.SF.diGly.Protein <- MSstats.SF.diGly.Protein %>% filter(str_detect(Protein, "_"))

Essentially this removes data without any '_' symbol, which you only get if it is followed by a diGly site e.g. Ttn would be removed and Ttn_K6 would be kept. 

Any advice on what the best approach and best time to removing unmodified peptides would be greatly appreciated :) 

Many thanks

Sam

messages.author: 6597c45f2a31b5d0
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM removing unmodified peptides
parts:
Hi Sam,

The way you removed the unmodified peptides after protein summarization should be adequate.  From what I've seen with many MSstatsPTM converters is that users can define which specific modification they're interested in, causing the converter to remove the unmodified peptides by default.

Out of curiosity, which converter did you use (e.g. MaxQuant, Progenesis, etc.)?  

Tony

messages.author: 5ccb721d28384a05
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM removing unmodified peptides
parts:
Hi Tony,

I used proteome discoverer, this was the code I used which did not remove unmodified peptides by default

msstats_input.SF <- PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat(
  raw.pd.SF.digly,
  annotation = annotation.pd.SF.digly,
  protein_input = raw.pd.SF,
  annotation_protein = annotation.pd.SF,
  fasta_path = "UP000000589_mouse_proteome.fasta",
  mod_id = "\\(GG\\)",
  labeling_type = "TMT",
  use_localization_cutoff = FALSE,
  which_proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions")

Thanks

Sam
